newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles offers police chief $375,000 buyout.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles offers police chief $375,000 buyout.

text.p: Los Angeles City Council on Tuesday agreed to offer beleaguered police chief Willie Williams a $375,000 severance package that would allow him to leave office almost two months early.
The city's police commission decided in March not to renew Williams' five-year contract for a second term, citing a poor job performance rating.
The buyout offer, negotiated by a special mediator, retired Los Angeles County Superior Court Judge Richard Byrne, was sent to Williams' lawyers.
While there was no immediate response to the offer, Mayor Richard Riordan said Williams' attorneys, in prior negotiations, had given Byrne, "every reason to believe they would accept the settlement."

Under the agreement Williams, the first African American to serve as the police chief of America's second largest city, cannot sue the city for the termination of his employment, as he had threatened to do.
In addition, he will be able to start drawing on his pension benefits immediately he leaves office, rather than having to wait until 2001.

Williams was brought in from Philadelphia in 1992 as a "model" chief to revamp a department sullied by the police beating of black motorist Rodney King and the riots that ensued when the four white officers involved were cleared of wrongdoing by a jury. He was given a poor rating by the police commission when it evaluated his job performance.
The commission, in turning down the chief's second term, said it had problems with Williams' management ability and his integrity -- sentiments expressed by a number of council members.
Under the buyout plan, Williams will leave office on May 17 rather than staying on until his term ends on July 7, allowing the process of picking a replacement to move ahead quickly.
